Which marcher lordships fell is not on the pages (confidence 1). [Fix eu-11-x, 2026-10-25] The single 1404-1409 contest over the whole March is split in three zones that end when the rebels lose them.

region.text: the rest of the March (Powys, Brecknock, Denbighshire)

ledger.note: 1404: Glyndwr's own country. The rising began at Sycharth in 1400; 'Powys adhered to the rising' (Owain page, autumn 1400); which lordships he held is not on the page (confidence 1).

May 1405: the rebels lose the south-east. Owain page: in early 1405 the Welsh 'suffered a series of defeats'; Pwll Melyn 'in May 1405'. The Glyndwr Rising page places the defeats at Grosmont and Usk 'in the south east of Wales' in 1406 (it calls the same defeat 'Early in 1406'); the two pages disagree by a year and this dossier takes the Owain page's 1405.
By 1407: 'the English had recaptured Anglesey and large parts of south Wales' (Glyndwr Rising page, lead); 'One by one the Lordships began to surrender' after the July 1407 submissions.

1407: 'the superior numbers, resources, and wealth that England had at its disposal began to turn the tide of the war' (Owain page); by 1409 only 'Harlech and Aberystwyth' were left, so the March is clear of the rebels by 1407-1408; a bridge, confidence 1.

notes: No Cliopatria row. The Marcher lordships were about 140 separate lordships (no page opened gives a count) and the region choices are county-level; the Gwynedd dossier lists marcher-lordships as counterpart for gains in 1215, 1234, 1257 and 1260 (Builth, Brecon, Gwrtheyrnion) that are not mirrored here because no page for them was opened. The lordship of Brecon (requested by eu-11-d as lordship-of-brecon, 1093) and the Lordship of Glamorgan are inside this dossier; Cliopatria's Norman England row adds 35 cells in mid and south-west Wales from 1085. Type state is a convention: the March was 'to a greater or lesser extent independent of both the English monarchy' and of the Principality. The first lordships came with the earldoms of Chester, Shrewsbury and Hereford 'Immediately after the Norman Conquest' (no year); start 1071 is the first dated castle. [Fix eu-11-x, 2026-10-25] After the review: (1) Powys is no longer drawn whole: it is cut by the Cliopatria shapes of the two Powys dossiers until 1284 and the whole county returns in 1284 (Powys Wenwynwyn page); (2) the 1197 gain of Ceredigion and the 1283 loss of Ceredigion are dropped (the quoted sentence concerns Rhys ap Tewdwr, 1093; see deheubarth); (3) Gwynedd's gains from the March: only 1234/6 (Builth and the upper Wye, 7 H3 cells) touches the cells held here, 1260/1 repeats the same cells, and 1215/12 and 1257 fall outside this shape, so one loss and one 1277/11 return are recorded; (4) years and counterparts aligned: Gwent 1086 from kingdom-of-morgannwg, Glamorgan c. 1090 from kingdom-of-morgannwg, Brecknock April 1093 from kingdom-of-brycheiniog, Radnorshire about 1100 from nobody, Denbighshire 1284 from kingdom-of-england, north Powys 1284 from kingdom-of-powys-wenwynwyn; the owners of kingdom-of-morgannwg (1086 and 1090 losses), kingdom-of-brycheiniog (1093/4 loss to lordship-of-brecon), kingdom-of-gwynedd (1136 gain from norman-england) and kingdom-of-powys-wenwynwyn (1284 loss to kingdom-of-england) should rename those counterparts to marcher-lordships; (5) the 1404-1409 contest is split into three zones that end in 1405, 1407 and 1407 as the rebels lose them (mirrored in glyndwr-s-wales). How norman-england and this dossier divide the March: Cliopatria's Norman England row (1085 onward, 35 cells in Wales) and the norman-england dossier draw the same conquests as English land; this dossier draws the Norman-held Wales from 1071 as one state, so the compiler should let these keyframes win over the Norman England cells in Wales and treat Radnorshire, Brecknock, Glamorgan and Gwent as March, not as England. The 1283 Denbighshire event is now dated by the Lordship of Denbigh page (1284), no longer a bridge. The Powys cut also uses the Kingdom of Powys shape of 1099 (the first Cliopatria shape of 1099-1151), and Brecknock is the Kingdom of Brycheiniog's Cliopatria shape (1072-1084, cut to Wales) without the Powys shapes.
